# LLM Post-Training Theory Conversation

[← Scale AI](../README.md) · [Every Scale AI question](../../scale-ai.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/llm-post-training-theory-conversation)

`domain-knowledge` `ml-knowledge` `transformer`

---

## Round outline

- Format: oral questions and answers, with approximately one hour allotted to the onsite MLE theory interview.
- Covered areas include:
  - Dropout.
  - L1 versus L2 regularization.
  - Tokenization, with particular attention to the trade-off between vocabulary size and sequence length.
  - Supervised fine-tuning: its training objective and how the data is prepared.
  - RL / preference optimization: DPO, GRPO, PPO, how the methods differ, and how they compare.
- Related MLE screens may also test wider post-training fundamentals.

## Guidance

- Study both the definitions and the trade-offs, since interviewers may shift rapidly from introductory to advanced questions.
- For tokenization, relate vocabulary size to embedding-table size, sequence length, compression, rare-token behavior, and latency downstream.
- For SFT, be prepared to explain prompt / response formatting, loss masking, quality filtering, and why preparing the data can matter as much as choosing the optimizer.
- For DPO / GRPO / PPO, concentrate on the signal consumed by each approach, whether a reward model is required, and the trade-offs involving stability and implementation.

## Study plan

- Create a one-page comparison chart for DPO, GRPO, and PPO covering the objective, required data, reward-model requirement, stability, and implementation complexity.
- Practice a brief explanation of tokenization trade-offs using one numerical example that includes vocabulary size and sequence length.
- Refresh dropout and L1/L2 regularization through their equations and their practical effects during training.
